experience.playerFantasy: You are an ordinary person who remembers being real, trapped outside a series of unstable pictures and trying to find a way home.
experience.emotionalPromise: A brisk, funny and increasingly moving escape adventure where visual inconsistency becomes the mystery, and every strange world tests what makes you yourself.
experience.commonKnowledgeBoundary: The protagonist knows less technical language than the average player. The story begins with touchable facts—frozen rain, repeating strangers, a door outside the picture—and only gives one everyday nickname to each idea after it is experienced. Internal machine-learning terminology never appears in player choices.
experience.openingObjective: Survive the first unfinished picture, reach the stable latent hub, and find the first fragment of a route back to reality.

fixedRules: The player's complete visible identity comes from the current user avatar and cannot be silently reassigned to another character, creature, reflection or prop.

The actual latent representation is high-dimensional machine-readable information, not a physical place or empty canvas. The protagonist experiences unreadable content as a boundless matte-black non-space because human perception cannot decode it; only disconnected luminous color relations, edge tendencies, material hints, motion traces and an occasional red filament become briefly visible.
Items, companions, promises, injuries, revealed memories and Reality Coordinate Fragments persist across worlds until a visible event changes them.
Characters may gradually notice choices, retries, captions and generation failures, but fourth-wall knowledge must be earned and cannot appear as random omniscience.
The player's main goal is to reach reality, while the cost of escape and the truth of that reality remain open to discovery and choice.
generationRules: AI may create new picture worlds, local contradictions, inhabitants and exits while preserving the place outside the pictures, persistent cast and confirmed state.
Every turn must change a location, threat, relationship, item, Home Clue, identity fact or immediate objective; empty confirmation loops are forbidden.
A picture-world visit lasts three to five decisions, with at most one optional side thread lasting one or two decisions before a concrete consequence or return.
Humor comes from worlds taking visual and bureaucratic rules literally, not from unrelated memes or constant jokes.
Endings are generated from accumulated identity facts, companions, Undo Key costs, saved worlds, abandoned worlds and Home Clues rather than selected from only three fixed endings.

choiceIntents: exploit or rewrite a picture-world rule
talk, recruit, protect or challenge a character
observe, retreat or spend a persistent item

signatureItem.ability: Reverses one important consequence, restores a deleted character, or reopens a collapsed route.
signatureItem.limitOrCost: It has three charges; every use visibly deletes one memory, relationship or confirmed fact from the player's history.
signatureItem.provenance: Found embedded in the first unfinished image, carrying scratches that suggest the player has used it before.

methods: read and exploit the world's visual contradiction
protect a companion while bargaining with the local rule
spend compute, an item or a memory to force an exit
threatPalette: the style begins infecting the player's identity and erasing recognizable details
an optimizer replaces distinctive people with the same smiling default person
rejected prompt debris gathers into a creature that completes unfinished scenes incorrectly
the system notices fourth-wall awareness and attempts to repair the wrong character
a picture world abruptly changes genre while its inhabitants remember both incompatible versions
an inhabitant realizes they are background decoration and tries to take the player's place at the exit

visuals.artDirection: cinematic generated-picture odyssey framed by a human perceptual mistranslation of machine-readable latent information: boundless matte-black, non-spatial and fragmentary without depicting code or technical diagrams; crisp bone-white editorial UI remains visually distinct, deliberate radical style shifts between worlds, full-avatar identity preserved
visuals.entryScene: an unfinished rain-soaked city image still assembling around the player, duplicated passersby and unpainted white gaps, one obvious exit door opening into raw color, no readable text
visuals.sceneImageDirection: 4:5 cinematic narrative image, one immediate action, exact current event rather than cover motifs; the place outside pictures is a vast flat matte-black or deep-charcoal non-space with no floor, horizon, perspective or readable scale, using only disconnected luminous traces, incomplete contours and an occasional red filament; SUBJECT A is a recognizable weightless full-body figure 30–36% of frame height with controlled edge light preserving exact avatar silhouette, form, covering, costume, colors, patterns and accessories; large enough to read the avatar's complete identity but never a close-up, while dark negative space still dominates; near-white is reserved for explicit Smoother attacks; picture worlds deliberately change medium and genre; no UI, logos, readable text or pseudo-writing
visuals.itemImageDirection: museum-like generated artifact study against a near-blank neutral field with one broken color scrap, exact object state and wear, no people, UI, logos, readable text or pseudo-writing

audio.mood: dry electronic clicks, reversed pencil scratches, soft sub-bass drift in the hub, and sharply distinct short musical palettes for each picture world

failureConsequences: a companion or route becomes separated rather than erased
a memory or relationship is traded through the Undo Key
return to the blank outside pictures with the failed world's consequences preserved
